ets1.next_step: Parliament and Council begin negotiating the Commission's July 2026 targeted ETS revision proposal (Phase 5, 2031–2040, aligned to the 2040 climate target).
ets1.notes: Core ETS has run since 2005 (currently Phase 4). On 17 July 2026 the Commission tabled a targeted revision covering post-2030 rules — a new, parallel process still at proposal stage; it doesn't change the base law's own status.

ets2.next_step: Member states continue building ETS2 registries and reporting infrastructure ahead of the trading launch.
ets2.notes: Trading start was postponed by one year, from 2027 to 2028, alongside the EU's 2040 climate target law (adopted March 2026), citing household/business cost concerns amid high energy prices.

cbam.next_step: Importers continue quarterly emissions tracking under the definitive regime; first annual declarations are due in 2027.
cbam.notes: The definitive regime started on schedule on 1 January 2026 — not delayed, unlike several other laws on this list. Over 4,100 CBAM declarants were registered at launch.
cbam.omnibus_note: Omnibus I introduced a 50-tonne annual mass "de minimis" threshold exempting roughly 90% of importers (mostly SMEs and individuals) from CBAM obligations, via amending procedure 2025/0039(COD) — Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, in force 20 October 2025.

red3.next_step: Commission pursues infringement proceedings against member states with incomplete transposition; remaining states finalize national laws.
red3.notes: The EU transposition deadline passed in May 2025, but several member states still hadn't fully transposed by mid-2026; Greece, Malta and Portugal were referred to the CJEU in April 2026.

csddd.next_step: Member states must transpose the revised directive; the Commission is to issue delegated acts and implementation guidance.
csddd.notes: Heavily amended by the 'Omnibus I' simplification package (in force March 2026). The transposition deadline was pushed twice — substantive company compliance obligations now don't start until 2029.
csddd.omnibus_note: Omnibus I first postponed transposition/application via a 'stop-the-clock' procedure (Directive (EU) 2025/794, April 2025), then substantively narrowed scope and liability rules via a further amendment (Directive (EU) 2026/0470, published 26 February 2026).

crma.next_step: Continued rollout of Strategic Projects and progress toward the 2030 extraction/processing/recycling benchmarks.
crma.notes: A February 2026 European Court of Auditors report concluded implementation is 'unlikely to deliver the targeted supply security' on its current trajectory.

nzia.next_step: Continued designation of Net-Zero Strategic Projects and rollout of resilience criteria toward the 40% domestic manufacturing goal.
nzia.notes: In force and implementing since mid-2024. See the CCUS entry for the Article 23 CO2 storage-capacity target specifically.

csrd.next_step: Wave 2 and Wave 3 companies prepare for reporting under the new thresholds; simplified ESRS standards are being finalized.
csrd.notes: Substantially narrowed by Omnibus I (thresholds raised to >1,000 employees / >€450M turnover). Wave 1 (the largest companies) has reported since FY2024; Waves 2–3 were delayed to FY2027/FY2028.
csrd.omnibus_note: Same Omnibus I amendment as CSDDD raised the scope threshold to >1,000 employees / >€450M turnover and delayed Wave 2/3 reporting; final act Directive (EU) 2026/0470, published 26 February 2026.

taxonomy.next_step: Companies apply the new simplified reporting templates for FY2026, with a transitional option for FY2025.
taxonomy.notes: A simplifying Delegated Act (part of Omnibus) cut required data points by roughly 64% for non-financial and 89% for financial undertakings.
taxonomy.omnibus_note: A Commission Delegated Act adopted 4 July 2025 (in force 1 January 2026) cut mandatory Taxonomy reporting data points by ~64% for non-financial undertakings and ~89% for credit institutions — done via delegated act, not a new legislative procedure, so the base regulation's own procedure reference is unchanged.

sfdr.next_step: Parliament finalizes its negotiating position on 'SFDR 2.0' before trilogues with Council and the Commission begin.
sfdr.notes: Current SFDR remains fully in force. A revision ('SFDR 2.0') is underway: Commission proposal Nov 2025 (procedure 2025/0361(COD)), Council mandate adopted June 2026; trilogues expected toward the end of 2026.
sfdr.omnibus_note: The 'SFDR 2.0' revision is a separate track (procedure 2025/0361(COD)), not part of Omnibus I — OEIL does not label it as an Omnibus file, unlike the CBAM/CSRD/CSDDD amendments.

eudr.next_step: Operators build out due-diligence systems ahead of the new application date; the Commission finalizes a scope-narrowing delegated act.
eudr.notes: Application date delayed twice — now December 2026 for large/medium operators (June 2027 for micro/small). The Commission's May 2026 review said the law itself won't be reopened, but proposed scope changes to cut compliance costs.
eudr.omnibus_note: The application-date delay (Regulation (EU) 2024/3234) and scope-narrowing amendment (Regulation (EU) 2025/2650) are EUDR-specific simplification tracks, not part of Omnibus I — neither carries an 'Omnibus' label on OEIL.

nature-restoration.next_step: Member states finalize and submit draft National Restoration Plans to the Commission.
nature-restoration.notes: A December 2025 assessment found implementation underway in most member states, but progress uneven against the binding 2030/2050 targets.

lulucf.next_step: Member states track performance against the new binding 2026–2029 LULUCF budgets en route to individual 2030 targets.
lulucf.notes: The EU-wide net land sink remains well below the 2030 target of -310 MtCO2e, raising delivery concerns among independent analysts. The OEIL reference cited is for the 2023 amending regulation; the original 2018 LULUCF procedure was not separately pulled.

ccus.next_step: Obligated oil & gas producers continue developing CO2 storage capacity; the Commission is expected to table a CO2 transport-network legal framework later in 2026.
ccus.notes: Tracked via the Net-Zero Industry Act's Article 23 (no standalone CCUS law) — same OEIL procedure as NZIA. Storage capacity is growing, but the transport-network framework needed to hit the 50 Mt/year 2030 target is still pending.

eed.next_step: Member states and covered entities apply energy management and audit requirements; the Commission continues supporting guidance.
eed.notes: The national transposition deadline passed in October 2025; focus is now on enforcement and compliance monitoring toward the binding 11.7% energy-reduction target by 2030.
